content: The UC Davis School of Medicine was established in 1966 and graduated its first class of physicians in 1972. While the school maintains research facilities on the Davis campus, the majority of its teaching and clinical activities are conducted in Sacramento, which is located 17 miles east of Davis. In December 2006, the school opened a new Education Building, marking the transition of all medical school classes to the Sacramento campus. Research activities, however, continue to take place on both campuses and are expected to do so in the foreseeable future. The admissions process at UC Davis School of Medicine is highly competitive due to its small class size, desirable location in Northern California, and relatively affordable tuition. In 2005, the school received 4,109 applications, of which 392 applicants were invited for interviews, and 93 ultimately matriculated. This results in an acceptance rate of approximately 6%. In 2007, the school was ranked 30 in primary care and 49 in research by U.S. News & World Report. The UC Davis Medical Center, located in Sacramento, is one of five teaching hospitals within the University of California system. It is recognized as one of the top 50 hospitals in the United States, according to an annual survey by U.S. News & World Report. Other hospitals affiliated with the UC Davis School of Medicine include the UC Davis Children’s Hospital, the UC Davis Cancer Center, Shriners Hospitals for Children-Northern California, and the Sacramento VA Medical Center. The faculty at the UC Davis School of Medicine are engaged in a broad spectrum of research, encompassing areas such as neuroscience, cancer biology, vascular biology, genetic diseases, functional genomics, health services, infectious diseases, nutrition, telemedicine, and vision science. The school receives approximately $90 million annually in funding from the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Additionally, about half of the medical students at UC Davis participate in research during their training. These clinics not only deliver high-quality healthcare to patients but also offer medical students valuable hands-on clinical experience early in their training. Notable student-run clinics include Clinica Tepati, the Imani Clinic at Oak Park, the Joan Viteri Memorial Clinic, the Paul Hom Asian Clinic, and the Shifa Community Clinic.
